# VIX Trading Strategies

This note documents the primary implied volatility trading strategies for $VIX products. It is an evergreen reference — not a live trade setup. Live applications are recorded in dated chart analysis or observation notes and linked back here.

---

## Term Structure — The Master Signal

The $VIX futures term structure determines whether any VIX position has structural support:

| Structure | Shape | Condition | What it means |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Contango (normal)** | Upward-sloping (front < back) | Bull/flat market | Futures at premium to $VIX; decay drag on long vol products; favors short-vol (SVXY) |
| **Backwardation (inverted)** | Downward-sloping (front > back) | Fear regime | Futures at discount to $VIX; no decay drag; long vol products gain structural edge |

**Critical rule:** Do not buy UVIX, VXX, or UVXY when VIX futures are trading at a premium to $VIX — the term-structure drag will erode any long position.

---

## Strategy 1 — Simple Long Volatility Speculation

**When to use:** VIX futures premium to $VIX = zero or negative (futures at parity or discount).

**Instruments:**
- Buy call options on $VIX futures (Cboe-listed; underlying is the VIX futures contract, NOT spot VIX)
- Buy UVIX (2x VIX futures ETN) or VXX calls — short-term only; roll forward at expiry

**Key constraint:** Stay at most one month out in time. Intermediate-term VIX ETFs (VIXM) lose value in all market conditions due to structural roll costs. The rule: front-month only, roll if it expires.

**Signal trigger:** When the VIX futures premium goes to zero or negative, UVIX no longer has a structural drag and two-sided upside returns are possible.

---

## Strategy 2 — VIX Futures Calendar Spread (Term Structure Trade)

**When to use:** Expecting the term structure to invert (or invert further), i.e., expecting a fear escalation.

**Structure:**
- **Buy** front-month $VIX futures
- **Sell** second-month $VIX futures

**Risk:** Unlimited — term structure can revert rapidly, reversing the spread. Requires considerable margin. Not recommended for retail without constant monitoring.

**Options equivalent:** Buy a front-month VIX call / sell a second-month VIX call. Brokerage margin is assessed as naked on the short leg because the two expirations don't behave like a standard options calendar.

---

## Strategy 3 — VIX/SPY Hedge (Discount Capture)

**When to use:** Front-month $VIX futures trading at a steep discount to spot $VIX (typically ≥ 3.00 points below). This occurs during or just after major fear events.

**Structure:**
- Buy 2 slightly ITM $VIX calls
- Buy 1 slightly ITM SPY call

**Logic:** $VIX and SPY move inversely. Owning both creates a quasi-long straddle. The VIX futures discount must narrow to zero by expiration — capturing that convergence is the edge. SPY calls hedge against $VIX falling back.

**Roll/exit rule:**
- Roll either leg up if it becomes deeply in-the-money
- Remove entire spread when $VIX futures begin trading at a premium to $VIX again

**Historical setup conditions:** October 2008, March 2020, April 2025 (to a lesser extent).

---

## Strategy 4 — Short Volatility via SVXY

**When to use:** Term structure upward-sloping (contango confirmed) AND $VIX futures at healthy premiums to $VIX.

**Instrument:** SVXY (inverse $VIX ETN) or calls on SVXY.

**Do NOT use when:** Term structure is inverted or $VIX futures are at a discount. April 2025 equity decline was a clear SVXY avoid condition.

**Exit signal:** When futures begin to trade at a premium again (post-fear normalization), re-entry into SVXY is appropriate.
